The best kind of snow blower to use on gravel is a two-stage model. The auger on a single-stage snow blower makes contact with the ground, so it will pick up gravel and throw it. A two-stage or three-stage snow blower has an intake that is elevated above the ground, allowing it to pick up snow without disturbing the gravel beneath it. Three-stage models work similarly, but they are heavy-duty options generally used by professionals.

Blinds vs. Shades: How to Choose the Right Option for Your Home

⏱️ ~8 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways

  • Sometimes, updating a room can be as simple as updating the window treatments for a quick facelift.
  • Sources indicate that blinds and shades are the two popular options, each with their own advantages in interior design and function.

Sometimes, updating a room can be as simple as updating the window treatments for a quick facelift. The right choice can give you a sleek, modern aesthetic or a softer, more inviting atmosphere. But it’s not all just looks, they also control natural light, maintain privacy, and can even improve your home’s energy efficiency.

Sources indicate that blinds and shades are the two popular options, each with their own advantages in interior design and function. So, which one is right for your space? From design preferences and trends to the practical things like maintenance and insulation, we’ll take a look at the pros and cons of blinds vs. shades to help you find the perfect fit for your home.

It has been revealed that shades and blinds are both hung within (or just outside) the top of a window frame, and extend to the bottom of the glass pane, but the window coverings differ in the way they’re constructed. Blinds are composed of individual slats made from hard materials like wood, aluminum, or vinyl. These slats can be tilted to control the amount and direction of sunlight entering a room. Most blinds can also be raised or pulled to the side to fully expose the window.

In a recent development, window shades, on the other hand, are generally made from a continuous piece of fabric or another flexible material that rolls, folds, or stacks when raised. They give a softer appearance and come in a variety of styles, from light-filtering roller shades to insulating cellular shades.

Blinds.com’s blackout cellular shade provides privacy and insulation; customize it as motorized, top down/bottom up, or corded/cordless.

According to recent reports, blinds and shades have their own advantages, so there isn’t an outright winner for every home. Blinds give you more control over light and privacy, while shades can look softer and have insulating properties. Here’s a breakdown of the pros and cons of each.

It has been revealed that the right window treatment depends on more than just how they look. Before deciding between blinds and shades, consider how you use the room, how much natural light you want, and how much maintenance you’re willing to take on. These key factors can help narrow down your options.

Blinds and shades will both provide privacy, but they each do it differently. Blinds give you more flexibility throughout the day. You can angle the slats to block the view from outside without completely closing off the light from the window. This makes them practical for living rooms, home offices, and other spaces where you want some natural light without feeling exposed.

Shades give you privacy when they’re lowered, but the amount of privacy will depend on the fabric. Sheer and light-filtering materials can provide privacy during the day, but will show silhouettes at night when your lights are on. Room-darkening and blackout shades are better for bedrooms and bathrooms, where privacy is definitely a must.

Blinds.com’s premium roller shade blocks UV rays and preserves views, and is available in a variety of patterns, colors, and fabrics.

According to recent reports, for precise control over how much sunlight gets through the window, blinds have the upper hand. The adjustable slats let you redirect sunlight up at the ceiling or away from a TV or computer screen, reducing glare while still keeping some natural light.

Shades are different. Light-filtering fabrics soften the harsh sunlight and give a gentle glow, while blackout shades are designed to block most incoming light. That stated, shades don’t really let you fine-tune as much as blinds. For more flexibility, try top-down/bottom-up shades, which can be lowered from the top or raised from the bottom, or dual shades that use both light-filtering and blackout materials.

It has been revealed that cost for both blinds and shades will depend on the materials, size, and additional features. Basic vinyl or aluminum blinds tend to be the most budget-friendly options, so they’re practical if you’re looking to cover multiple windows without spending a fortune.

Shades can also be affordable, assuming you’re looking at simple roller shades made from synthetic fabrics. However, premium Roman shades, double-cell cellular shades, and custom fabric options will cost more.

For either option, custom sizing, professional installation, and motorized or smart controls can significantly inflate the price tag. Standard-sized, manually operated window treatments are usually the cheapest choice.

It has been revealed that window treatments can also help keep your home comfortable throughout the year. When it comes to insulation, however, certain types of shades have a clear advantage.

Cellular shades are particularly effective thanks to their honeycomb construction, which traps air in pockets between the window and the room. This helps reduce heat loss during winter and heat gain during summer, potentially lowering your energy bills. Roman shades with insulating liners can also provide some thermal benefits.

Sources indicate that blinds can help reduce solar heat gain by blocking or redirecting direct sunlight, but gaps between the slats don’t give you much insulation. If energy efficiency is one of your priorities, well-fitted cellular shades may be your best bet.

It has been revealed that older blinds and shades have long pull or loop cords, which are a serious strangulation hazard to young children and pets. Luckily, today’s options are much safer, with cordless designs becoming the standard for both blinds and shades.

There was even an update to window-covering safety standards in June 2024, which restricted hazardous cords on custom window coverings even more. Thanks to this change, you can now choose from a wide range of cordless and motorized options in both categories.

Sources indicate that according to the U.S. Consumer Product Safety Commission, cordless window coverings are the safest choice for homes with young children. If you still have older cord-operated blinds or shades, replacing them with cordless alternatives is recommended.

These fabric vertical blinds from Blinds.com filter harsh sunlight and are durable, cost-effective alternatives to drapes.

Window treatments can have a surprising impact on the look and feel of a room. If you’re wondering how to dress a window without curtains, both blinds and shades give you plenty of stylish options. Blinds have a structured, tailored appearance that works well in modern, minimalist, and traditional interiors. Wood and faux wood blinds can add warmth and natural texture, while aluminum blinds look great in industrial or modern spaces.

It has been revealed that shades have a little more variety in terms of fabric, color, pattern, and texture. Roman shades can create an elegant, layered look, while simple roller shades are ideal for a clean, understated aesthetic. Woven wood shades made from bamboo or other natural materials can give organic texture and complement coastal, bohemian, or rustic spaces.

According to recent reports, of course, it will all come down to your own preference and the atmosphere you’re trying to create. Blinds are ideal for a crisp, structured look, while shades can make a room feel softer and more inviting.

In a recent development, in general, blinds are easier to maintain than shades. The hard surfaces are easy to dust or wipe down with a damp cloth, so they’re a great choice for kitchens, bathrooms, and other areas where moisture or splashes are common. Just keep in mind, though, that cleaning each individual slat can take time.

Fabric shades need a gentler approach. Most can be vacuumed with a brush attachment, while certain materials can be spot-cleaned. More delicate fabrics may need professional cleaning, and exposure to sunlight can cause some materials to fade over time.

In a busy house, low-maintenance blinds or easy-clean roller shades may be the most practical options.

WIth so many options, the material and configuration you choose can affect everything from durability to how much sunlight enters the room. Here are some of the most common types of blinds to consider:.

Shades come in a huge range of styles, from simple designs to decorative options that can be more of a focal point in the room. Some of the most popular types include:.

In a recent development, when choosing between blinds and shades, the decision comes down to what you want in your space. If precise light control, durability, and easy cleaning are your priorities, blinds are probably best. If you prefer a softer aesthetic, better insulation, or room darkening, shades may be worth the extra cost.

According to recent reports, remember, you don’t have to commit to one type of window treatments and use it throughout the home. Use blinds for high-traffic areas like kitchens and home offices, and shades for bedrooms and living spaces where comfort and aesthetics are more of a priority. Mixing and matching window treatments can help you strike the right balance between style, functionality, and budget.

Border Search of Immigration Lawyer's Phone Was Likely Unconstitutional Retaliation for Lawyer's Speech

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that andrew Lattarulo is an immigration lawyer and part owner of the law firm Georges Cote LLP, which represents "thousands of clients in active immigration proceedings." Lattarulo also runs a popular Instagram account featuring videos of himself discussing "know-your-rights information about U.S.
  • It has been revealed that audai Cote, "the registered agent and individual in charge of I-9 compliance" at the firm, was served with a Notice of Inspection on September 8, 2025.
  • In late September 2025, while the HSI investigation proceeded, both Lattarulo and Cote travelled from Boston to Aruba for a weekend trip.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

From Judge Allison Burroughs (D. Mass.) Friday in Lattarulo v. Mullin:.

Sources indicate that andrew Lattarulo is an immigration lawyer and part owner of the law firm Georges Cote LLP, which represents "thousands of clients in active immigration proceedings." Lattarulo also runs a popular Instagram account featuring videos of himself discussing "know-your-rights information about U.S. immigration matters," which regularly "amasses hundreds of thousands of views." Georges Cote is currently being investigated by Homeland Security Investigations ("HSI"), the investigative arm of the Department of Homeland Security ("DHS"), for employing individuals without a legal right to work in the United States.

It has been revealed that audai Cote, "the registered agent and individual in charge of I-9 compliance" at the firm, was served with a Notice of Inspection on September 8, 2025. Unlike Lattarulo, "Cote is not an immigration attorney—he focuses on personal injury." The firm responded on September 12, 2025, and the government sent Cote a Notice of Suspect Documents on September 25, 2025. The firm was given ten days to attempt to verify the identity and work authorization of the employees named in the Notice of Suspect Documents.

In late September 2025, while the HSI investigation proceeded, both Lattarulo and Cote travelled from Boston to Aruba for a weekend trip. On September 27, 2025, Cote arrived back at Logan Airport from Aruba without concern. Lattarulo made the same journey the following day, September 28, 2025. Lattarulo passed through customs preclearance in Aruba before boarding a flight to Boston.

When his flight arrived at Logan Airport, three U.S. Customs and Border Protection ("CBP") agents and one HSI officer stopped Lattarulo as he got off the plane. The agents seized his cell phone without a warrant and then downloaded a complete copy of the data stored on the phone. Eight days later, they returned the cell phone via overnight delivery.

Industry observers note that the seized cell phone data is presently in a format that is not readable or reviewable, but the government intends to convert the data to an accessible format and search it if the Court permits. The data includes confidential information, including privileged attorney-client communications related to Lattarulo's clients. {The Government was clear that any search of the contents of the phone would utilize a taint team to protect privileged information.} ….

The court held that Lattarulo was likely correct on his claim that the search was unconstitutional retaliation for his speech, and therefore granted "a preliminary injunction enjoining Defendants from accessing the data obtained from the phone before this action is resolved":.

"[T]he law is settled that as a general matter the First Amendment prohibits government officials from subjecting an individual to retaliatory actions, including criminal prosecutions, for speaking out." … The retaliation issue [here] turns on causation—that is, whether the seizure and search of Lattarulo's cell phone would have occurred but for his protected speech.

Sources indicate that respondents have provided no evidence that searches of cell phones are frequently conducted during the kind of employment investigation at glitch here, and Lattarulo has directed the Court to sources which suggest otherwise. Indeed, Lattarulo's evidence suggests that any pursuit of criminal charges against employers for employing unauthorized immigrants is exceedingly rare. The fact that the government, after Lattarulo spoke out publicly against it, elected to adopt a highly unusual investigative method that appears designed to inflict a maximal burden on Lattarulo lends substantial support to an inference that its actions were pretextual.

The stage of the investigation at which the search occurred further bolsters the inference of pretext. Under HSI's own policies, the agency "presumes that employers who, within 10 business days of receiving a Notice of Suspect Documents, verify the identity and/or employment authorization of the listed employees, or take appropriate actions to address the apparent employment of unauthorized workers, have demonstrated reasonable care under the INA." The government's search occurred only three days after Georges Cote first received a Notice of Suspect Documents, meaning that the agency was still early in its period of "presum[ing]" compliance when it occurred. Thus, the government's actions here required it to short-circuit its orderly investigative procedures and cast aside its ten-day presumption of compliance in favor of immediately seizing Lattarulo's phone. That aggressive deviation from protocol strongly suggests that the seizure did not arise from an ordinary investigative motive.

Sources indicate that further, Lattarulo has identified an "otherwise similarly situated individual not engaged in the same sort of protected speech," who was not subjected to the same enforcement action: his law firm partner Audai Cote, who had the same or greater access to the firm's employment records but did not speak publicly about immigrant rights. Indeed, if the government was truly intent on seizing evidence at the first possible opportunity, Mr. Cote, who returned to America a full day before Lattarulo, would have been a more logical target. Nonetheless, the government opted to wait until Lattarulo touched down in Boston the next day and subject only him to an intrusive cell phone search. The balance of the evidence currently before the Court thus suggests that Lattarulo is likely to establish that he would not have been searched except for his protected speech.

{It is true that the presence of probable cause generally precludes a finding of causation in a retaliatory arrest case, but the Supreme Court has recognized a limited exception for situations in which officers who "have probable cause to make arrests [for a particular crime] … typically exercise their discretion not to do so," such as "an individual who has been vocally complaining about police conduct … [before being] arrested for jaywalking," By analogy, the limited record before the Court suggests that searches of cell phones are not regularly conducted during the kind of employment investigation at issue here and that Lattarulo's own law firm partner was not subjected to the same seizure and search of property.}.

It is true that Defendants can "prevail … by showing that the [search] would have been initiated without respect to retaliation," and here Defendants state that they have additional evidence which would show as much, but they have not provided it because they assert that doing so would prejudice an ongoing investigation…. [T]he Court concludes that the limited record that is before the Court suggests that Lattarulo is likely to succeed on the merits of his First Amendment retaliation claim and that the record before it is therefore adequate to grant the limited preliminary relief contemplated by this order.

According to recent reports, the court didn't resolve Lattarulo's Fourth Amendment claim, because it granted the preliminary injunction based on the First Amendment claim. But it did note the following:.

Plaintiffs' Fourth Amendment claim turns largely on the scope of the border search exception to the Fourth Amendment's warrant requirement. That exception "is grounded in the government's 'inherent authority to protect, and a paramount interest in protecting, its territorial integrity.'" It allows the government to perform "routine" border searches of electronic devices without suspicion of any crime, and to perform "non-routine" border searches of electronic devices without a warrant, so long as the government has reasonable suspicion. Alasaad v. Mayorkas (1st Cir. 2021).

In a recent development, the question this case raises is: reasonable suspicion of what? In other words, what types of suspected criminal activities can the government use a warrantless advanced border search to investigate? The First Circuit in Alasaad stated that the exception applies to searches for "contraband" or for "evidence of contraband or a border-related crime." Later in its opinion, however, it stated that the exception applies to searches for "contraband, evidence of contraband, or for evidence of activity in violation of the laws enforced or administered by CBP or ICE." In most cases, of course, "border-related crime[s]" and "activity in violation of the laws enforced or administered by CBP or ICE" are synonymous, and the First Circuit in Alasaad appears to have intended to use those terms more or less synonymously.

The difficulty of this case lies in the fact that the suspected violation at matter—employment of unauthorized aliens in the United States in violation 8 U.S.C § 1324a—involves a law that is "enforced or administered by CBP or ICE" but arguably is not a "border-related crime." Based on the information before the Court, there appears to be no connection between Lattarulo's border crossing (or, more broadly, the government's interest in policing the border) and the suspected crime that formed the basis for the government's border search. Rather, it appears that the government seized on a fortuitous border crossing following a weekend vacation as an opportunity to search for evidence of a domestic crime it was already investigating.

Even though the suspected violation involves aliens and a law administered by ICE, the Court is not convinced that the First Circuit in Alasaad intended for the border exception to apply to investigations into activity that occurred nowhere near the border and that has no relationship to the border crossing during which the search occurred. Nor is the Court convinced that application of the border search exception to this type of investigation would further the principles underlying the exception. Nonetheless, given the novelty of these questions and the fact that a ruling on them is not necessary, the Court will refrain at this point from reaching a firm conclusion on the issue of the border search's applicability….

Mary Lemay and Patrick M. Hanley (Butters Brazilian LLP) represent Lattarulo.

That Hole in Your Ruler Isn’t Random – Here’s What It’s Actually For

📅 04 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (558 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Familyhandyman

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • That small hole on a ruler has a practical purpose and an unexpected history.
  • It has been revealed that almost everyone has used a ruler at some point, whether it was for a school project, measuring something around the house, or drawing a straight line.
  • It has been revealed that those holes in rulers aren’t just part of the design.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Family Handyman's Editorial Process.

That small hole on a ruler has a practical purpose and an unexpected history. Here's why it exists and how people use it.

It has been revealed that almost everyone has used a ruler at some point, whether it was for a school project, measuring something around the house, or drawing a straight line. But even after years of using one, there’s a small detail that’s easy to miss: the hole near the end.

It has been revealed that those holes in rulers aren’t just part of the design. They actually serve a purpose, and the reason they’re there goes back further than most people might expect. Here’s what they’re for, how they were used in the past, and a few other ways they come in handy.

Sources indicate that the hole at the end of a ruler is mainly there for storage. It lets people hang the ruler on a hook, nail, or pegboard instead of leaving it in a drawer or on a workbench. This is particularly helpful with longer metal rulers that might not fit in a toolbox.

In a recent development, but the hole has been around for much longer than modern workshops. Years ago, before paper notebooks became common in schools, students practiced writing on small slate boards. They could wipe away their writing with a damp cloth and use the board again.

Some students tied that cloth to their rulers with a piece of string through the hole. That way, they always had something nearby to clean their slates. Schools eventually moved away from slate boards, but the holes remained. Today, they’re mostly there to make rulers easier to hang and store.

Hanging a ruler isn’t the only reason manufacturers add holes. Some rulers have several, and they can serve different purposes depending on where they’re placed. For example, certain school rulers have three holes spaced along one side. These line up with the rings in a standard three-ring binder, so students can keep their rulers with their other school supplies.

In a recent development, some rulers also have holes that help with drawing circles. A pin through one hole can hold the ruler in place while a pencil in another hole traces a circle as the ruler turns. Not every ruler has holes designed for this, but specialty models like the Creative Grids Quick Trim Ruler do. A compass is still a better choice when exact measurements matter.

Sources indicate that some crafting rulers have holes for more specific jobs. Quilting rulers and templates may have openings that help mark circles or line up fabric before cutting. Others have slots or shaped edges that guide a rotary cutter, making it easier to cut certain shapes.

Industry observers note that there are also special rulers for paper crafts and stitching. Some have rows of tiny, evenly spaced holes that help people mark where to make stitches or decorative patterns.

According to recent reports, of course, not every ruler has holes. Smaller plastic rulers often don’t need them, while longer metal versions may have one at each end. It mostly comes down to how the manufacturer expects people to use the ruler. And for everyday measuring, the holes don’t make much difference. A ruler without them can measure just as accurately as one with them.

Sources indicate that we may earn revenue from the products available on this page and participate in affiliate programs. Learn More ›.

Industry observers note that caulk fixes myriad projects around the house, from outdoor maintenance to indoor decorating. What makes the material such a versatile DIY essential? The rubbery substance, available in a variety of formulations, including silicone, latex, acrylic, butyl rubber, polyurethane, and construction adhesives, can bond to almost any material, making it a wonderfully flexible material for projects indoors and out. With the right tube of caulk, you can solve just about any problem—including these common issues.

In a recent development, caulking windows and doors is the best way to reduce drafts, cut home energy costs, enhance your house’s energy efficiency, and decrease your carbon footprint, according to the Consumer Federation of America. For this job, choose either acrylic latex or vinyl latex caulk. Acrylic latex caulk works best in dry environments and will perform well for up to 15 years, while vinyl latex can be used in damp areas and lasts about 5 years.

Concrete and mortar repair caulk is an excellent tool for sealing cracks and gaps in concrete, brick, stucco, stone, and metal. Similarly, it’s perfect for repairing small fissures in foundations and basement walls that allow insects, rodents, and other pests to enter your home. Designed for both interior and exterior use, concrete and mortar repair caulk has a textured finish and can be painted once it’s dry.

No matter how carefully you measure and cut, you often end up with little gaps between, above, and below moldings and baseboards. When you need to close the gap, acrylic latex caulk is one of the best caulks for baseboards, ideal for filling in those small spaces. The product dries promptly and can be painted as soon as 6 to 8 hours after application. Acrylic latex also comes in a variety of different pigments, so you can match the color to the surrounding material.

Sources indicate that over time, small spaces can open up between tiles, and in moist environments that’s an invitation for mold and mildew to grow behind the walls. Both 100 percent silicone caulk and siliconized acrylic caulk are ideal for wet environments and form a durable, watertight seal. Mold- and mildew-resistant silicone caulk is made for nonporous surfaces like ceramic, glass, and metal, while waterproof siliconized acrylic caulk works well on tubs, tile, glass, and ceramic tile surfaces. Gorilla silicone sealant is ideal to use since it is waterproof, and mold and mildew resistant.

Gorilla silicone caulk is flexible, adheres well, and creates a mold- and mildew-resistant barrier on bathroom surfaces. Read the review.

Industry observers note that when you need to cover small holes and tiny cracks prior to painting, painter’s caulk, an acrylic latex compound, is just what you need. Painter’s caulk such as DAP Alex painter’s caulk adheres to wood, drywall, masonry, and other surfaces. Because it dries to a paintable texture in about an hour, it’s a good choice for busy DIYers.

In a recent development, fire barrier sealant, a specialized type of caulk, does more than patch holes. It actually helps make your home safer by preventing fire from moving through open spaces within a structure. Fire barrier sealant can be used to seal holes, gaps, and cracks around holes in interior framing, especially around plumbing or electrical conduits.

When a length of molding falls off, a corner of carpet comes up, or a tile comes loose, all-purpose caulk can often fix it. Dab a little caulk behind the loose piece, then stick it back into place. You can even use an all-purpose caulk like GE all-purpose silicone caulk to install wood wall paneling without nails.

To keep wallpaper from pulling up as it dries, run caulk along all trimmed paper seams, especially in the corners, then smooth with a wet sponge or finger to remove any surface imperfections. For wallpaper that is peeling, lift up the loose section of paper, apply adhesive under it, then smooth the paper back against the wall. Once the adhesive dries, apply a continuous bead of caulk along the seam to keep it from peeling up again.

With the right caulk, you can even repair a roof! Roof repair caulk, like Roofers Choice Roof Cement Caulk, can be used to seal small cracks or gaps along roof edges, between shingles, and around skylights or flashing. As you might expect, roof repair caulk is completely weatherproof and waterproof, and can be used in wet areas or on dry surfaces.

It has been revealed that as your home’s gutters age, they can develop cracks and gaps, especially around joints and downspout junctions. Butyl rubber caulk, a strong waterproof sealant, can be used to seal joints in those damaged gutters. Dab a little onto the cracks to keep your gutters leak-free—and keep rainwater flowing out and away from your home.

Painter’s caulk (or decorator’s caulk) is used, as its name suggests, just before decorating and painting. It’s the right choice for sealing crown molding, chair rails, and baseboards because it’s flexible and hides gaps between the wall and the finishes.

According to recent reports, whether you’re repairing a small hole or a sizable tear in your home’s vinyl siding, siding caulk can help. Simply choose a shade of exterior caulk that matches the hue of your exterior (even black caulk is available), and use a small dab to seal minor punctures, like nail holes. Cover larger holes or tears by applying caulk to the back of a scrap piece of siding, and covering the hole with the scrap piece.

According to recent reports, caulking between a countertop and a tile backsplash in the kitchen doesn’t just give your work space a “finished” look. It keeps crumbs, food items and worse yet, water, from getting behind your countertop and cabinets. Silicone caulk, which is moisture and mildew resistant, is the best caulk for the job. While you have your caulk gun out, make sure there’s a sturdy seal between your countertop and kitchen sink, too!

It has been revealed that when you don’t have any fluffy furniture pads on hand to stick on the undersides of flower pots and other decorative items, caulk can help. Turn your pots on their sides and apply a few dabs of silicone caulk to the bottoms of the pots. Allow the caulk to dry so the pots won’t stick to your floors. When they’re set, the silicone pads should keep the pot from scratching your hardwood.

One of the easiest ways to keep your asphalt or concrete driveway in good condition is to attend to cracks as soon as you notice them. The longer you wait, the better the chance that moisture will seep into the cracks, and make an even more fractured-looking mess of your driveway. Load your caulk gun with a quality, water-resistant asphalt crack sealant. Acrylic formulas are flexible and should fit into just about any nook or cranny.

#44160. Winter Storm Watch vs. Winter Storm Warning: What’s the Difference?

📅 04 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 3m • 📚 Deep Dive (658 w)

Gadgets 📈 Bullish 🌐 Familyhandyman ↗ Open Full Page

Winter Storm Watch vs. Winter Storm Warning: What’s the Difference?

📅 04 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (658 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Familyhandyman

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • A winter storm watch and winter storm warning mean different things.
  • In a recent development, tracking severe weather can sometimes feel like it requires a degree in meteorology.
  • Sources indicate that both alerts come from the National Weather Service, but they call for different levels of urgency.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Family Handyman's Editorial Process.

A winter storm watch and winter storm warning mean different things. Here's what each alert signals and how to prepare for dangerous weather.

In a recent development, tracking severe weather can sometimes feel like it requires a degree in meteorology. With complex scientific terms and technical jargon, it can be difficult to understand what it all means and what should be done to prepare. That’s when the difference between a winter storm watch and a winter storm warning matters.

Sources indicate that both alerts come from the National Weather Service, but they call for different levels of urgency. Here’s how the alerts work and what homeowners should do when they see one.

Industry observers note that A winter storm watch means a significant winter storm is possible, but forecasters aren’t yet sure where or when it will hit or how severe it will be. According to the National Weather Service, watches often arrive a day or two before a storm and can cover heavy snow, sleet, or ice.

It has been revealed that they give residents time to prepare, even though the storm may not reach their area. As the forecast becomes clearer, the National Weather Service may upgrade the watch to a warning, issue an advisory, or cancel it altogether.

Industry observers note that A winter storm warning means dangerous winter weather is expected or already happening. Heavy snow, sleet, or ice could make travel unsafe and cause other problems, including power outages. The amount of snow or ice needed to trigger a warning varies by location.

In a recent development, “Each office knows the local area and will matter Warnings, Watches or Advisories based on local criteria,” according to the National Weather Service. “For example, the amount of snow that triggers a ‘Winter Storm Warning’ in the Northern Plains is typically much higher than the amount needed to trigger a ‘Winter Storm Warning’ in the Southeast.”.

Warnings generally arrive closer to a storm’s arrival than watches, although forecasters can issue one before snow or ice begins falling.

Recent findings suggest that A winter weather advisory means snow, sleet, or ice is expected to cause problems, but forecasters don’t anticipate conditions severe enough for a warning. An advisory may signal slick roads or other travel disruptions. While the weather may be less severe than during a warning, residents should still take precautions and monitor local forecasts.

A winter storm watch gives homeowners time to prepare before conditions worsen. That includes checking heating systems, protecting exposed pipes from freezing, and stocking up on food, medications, and other essentials.

“Your primary concerns at home or work during a winter storm are loss of heat, power and telephone service and a shortage of supplies if storm conditions continue for more than a day,” according to the National Weather Service.

According to recent reports, homeowners should have flashlights, spare batteries, and a charged phone in case the power goes out. Checking smoke and carbon monoxide alarms, locating snow shovels, and stocking up on ice melt can also help.

Once a warning takes effect, homeowners should finish their preparations and avoid unnecessary travel. Staying indoors is generally safest during severe winter weather.

If the power goes out, residents can close off unused rooms and wear extra layers to stay warm. Portable generators should always remain outdoors, away from windows and doors. Grills and ovens should never serve as heating sources because they can create serious safety hazards.

In a recent development, residents should continue monitoring weather alerts throughout the storm. Once conditions improve, homeowners can check for damage and begin clearing snow and ice from walkways and driveways.

According to recent reports, national Weather Service, “Winter Weather Warnings, Watches and Advisories” National Weather Service, “Winter Weather Resources and Frequently Asked Questions” National Weather Service, “Prepare! Don’t Let a Winter Storm Take You by Surprise” Federal Emergency Management Agency, “Be Prepared for a Winter Storm”.
